text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

An all-women panel is not evidence of anything. Panels skew that way in many ministries simply because of who holds senior HR and policy roles; if a male-only panel picking a man wouldn't prove bias, the mirror image doesn't either. Raising it would also damage you: it reads as sour grapes and shifts attention from your actual grievance.

Your real issue is procedural. You asked for written reasons two weeks ago and got silence — that is concrete and defensible. Send a firm follow-up citing your right to a decision rationale, and ask specifically how the criteria were weighted and scored.

If the scoring then shows something odd — criteria invented late, or your experience discounted without explanation — that's worth pursuing. The panel's sex isn't.
